summary.short: Establishes principles, user rights and duties for internet use in Brazil. Covers net neutrality, personal data and log retention, intermediary liability for third-party content after court orders, and foreign providers serving Brazilians. In force 60 days after official publication.
summary.long: Law No. 12,965 of 23 April 2014 (Marco Civil da Internet) sets principles, user rights and duties for internet use in Brazil and guides public authorities at all levels (Arts. 1–3). It grants users privacy and communications protections, consent-based control of personal data, and clear contract terms (Art. 7). Network operators must treat traffic equally, allowing discrimination only for technical needs or emergency services, and must disclose traffic management (Art. 9). Connection providers keep connection logs for one year and application providers keep access logs for six months (Arts. 13, 15); other log and data retention is restricted (Arts. 14, 16). Disclosure of records requires prior judicial authorization (Arts. 10, 22–23). Application providers are liable for third-party content only after failing to remove it under a specific court order (Arts. 19–21). Public bodies receive governance, open-standard and e-government guidelines (Arts. 24–28). Breaches of Arts. 10–11 may incur warnings, fines of up to 10% of the Brazilian group's revenue, suspension or prohibition (Art. 12). Foreign providers serving Brazilian users are covered (Art. 11 §2). The law takes effect 60 days after official publication (Art. 32).

notes: The text is a consolidated reproduction with markers. Many provisions were inserted by MP 1.068/2021 and are marked '(Rejeitada)'; several are marked revoked. Some provisions (e.g., art. 5 VII-VIII and X, art. 7 X, art. 11 §2, art. 12, art. 16 II) appear twice, in original and amended wording. Coded relations and entities cover the operative text; MP-inserted provisions are cited only as amendment markers. The text states that it does not replace the official publication in the DOU of 24.4.2014. Art. 9 §1 and art. 11 §4 defer to unnamed regulations (decree). Art. 19 §2 defers to a future specific law for copyright; no such law is named.

obligations.summary: Users are assured clear and complete contract information on connection and application records, data protection and network management practices (Art. 7 VI). Art. 7 XIII is also a right, not a duty on a named addressee.
